frames.review_note: Small problems only. The silver chain of office hangs in a long loop down his back, so it looks worn back to front. The smoke is a row of several small plumes rather than one thin line, but it still reads as a distant line on the horizon. The sentry also has a topknot and moustache, but his mundu and crossed belts keep him distinct from Nagoji. Nagoji matches his sheet and the ch26 row: topknot, grey at the temples, curled moustache, clean chin, small gold ear stud, white coat over a red waistcoat with brass buttons, breeches and boots. There is no text in the art, and the open sky on the upper right takes both captions easily.

Minor only. Nagoji leans forward with both hands on the parapet instead of standing fully straight, but the alert posture still carries the beat. The sentry has stopped leaning, and two separate smoke columns stand far apart on the same horizon as 1.1. The tiled guard-house roof matches 1.1. Nagoji matches his sheet and bible row: topknot with no turban, grey temples, thick curled moustache, small gold ear stud, white coat, red waistcoat and silver chain. There is faint stipple on his jaw, but the chin reads clean-shaven. The sentry also has a topknot and moustache, like Nagoji, but his bare chest, crossed belts and mundu keep them distinct. The panel has no lettering. There is no painted text.

Small problems only. Ramayyan still faces Padmini with his stylus and has his back to the doorway, so only three of the four heads turn to the runner. Varma's hair knot sits at the back of his crown rather than above his left ear. Nagoji's ear stud reads pale rather than gold. Ramayyan shows a faint moustache that is not on his sheet. Otherwise the whole cast is present and on model: Padmini with grey in her coiled hair, gold, sari and stick; Ramayyan with receding hair, white cloth, stylus and palm leaves; Varma bare-headed and bare-chested in gold necklaces on the platform, spear beside him; Nagoji by a pillar in coat, red waistcoat and chain. The sweat-slick runner bursts through the main doorway. The cloth map has ink lines and no lettering. The lamps are brass with open wicks. Lettering placement: the caption can sit over the roof tiles at top centre, and the runner's balloon over the door lintel at top right.

Minor only. The foreground stick foot is drawn sharp instead of out of focus. It still hovers above the floor with its shadow below, so the 'stopped mid-tap' beat reads. Its rough bark texture matches Padmini's sheet but is rougher than the polished stick in 1.5. The floor has a glossy, slightly photographic finish. The runner matches 1.3: curly hair, moustache, sweat-slick bare chest and white loincloth. He kneels on his right knee with his right hand flat on the floor and his left foot planted. The anatomy is sound. The setting matches 1.3: dark carved pillars, brass lamps and an open doorway onto palms. There is no painted text. Lettering space: the plain dark wall and ceiling above the doorway (about x 0.31-0.62, y 0.02-0.19), with the empty lower floor as a second option.

Clean. It is a figureless high-angle view: pepper vines on rough posts on both sides of a narrow path, a canal with low cargo boats, and two small shrines half swallowed by foliage on the ridge. Two smoke trails rise, one from the northern hills and one from the coast. No figures (the boats are empty), no lettering and no anachronism. The lettering can sit in the sky band at the top and on the low-detail distant plain and sea at upper right. Varma is speaking off-panel from the hall, so his tail goes to the top edge.

Minor only. Ramayyan sits to the right across the table corner rather than squarely opposite. The ink-line map matches the script for 2.3, but 1.3 and 2.4 show a coloured map, so the map style varies across the page. Everything else matches: Nagoji in uniform (white coat, red waistcoat, brass buttons, silver chain, Kerala topknot with grey temples, curled moustache, clean chin, gold stud), Ramayyan matches his sheet with stylus and palm leaves, hands are sound, there is no lettering on the map, and the plain wall and roof at the top leave room for both balloons.

Minor only. The window is a tall barred opening rather than a narrow slit, and the rough stone-block wall differs from the plastered hall walls in 2.3 and 2.4, but the shot is tight enough to read as another corner of the fort. His fist covers his mouth and most of his chin; the visible jaw shows only faint ink texture, not a beard. Tight on Nagoji, lit from the side, two smoke columns on the horizon through the window, and a brooding expression that fits the beat. The uniform, topknot, grey temples, curled moustache and gold stud all match, and the hand is sound. The dark upper-left wall and the sky at upper right leave plenty of room for the caption and the 'Burn it.' balloon.

Minor only: the kneeling runner named in the art direction is not in frame (the hall-gone-still beat is still clear: Padmini's head snapped to Nagoji, Ramayyan and Varma frozen, guards at the doors). Varma's hair is a crown knot rather than the bible's side knot above the left ear, but this matches 1.3 and 2.4. Nagoji's breeches read as long trousers tucked into tall boots. Ramayyan's stylus rests on the leaf instead of hovering above it. Nagoji's face, stud, clean chin, uniform and the white scar on his left forearm are correct. The map is ink and wash only, with no lettering. Caption can sit top left over the roof beams and doorway; Padmini's small balloon fits on the dark wall between her head and Varma.

Minor only. This fixes every r1 problem. The brand on the inner left forearm is now a pale, puckered patch beside one long white scar, with no symbol or outline. The map is ink lines only (canal, dotted path, ridges, tiny trees) with no letters or pseudo-labels near the finger. There is no belt over the waistcoat. The doorway guards wear white head cloths and crossed belts, as in 3.1. Varma is seated on his dais at the right instead of an empty seat. Nagoji matches the sheet and the ch26 row: topknot, grey at the temples, thick curled moustache, clean chin, small gold ear stud, white coat, red waistcoat, brass buttons and silver chain. Both hands are sound, with the right index finger tracing the canal and the left palm flat. Small slips: Varma's hair is loose to the shoulders rather than in a knot, though he is small in the background. The map is plain ink while 3.1 and 3.3 show a colour-washed map, but the script asks for ink lines here. Both Nagoji balloons fit on the rafters and the cream wall at upper right, between the central pillar and Varma's window, or over the ceiling at upper left.

Acceptable, with background continuity slips worth noting. The r1 tattoo problem is gone: both of Nagoji's sleeves are down, so no forearm mark shows. The beat works. It is a two-shot across the map table: Padmini at left with her stick, grey threading through hair coiled at the nape, gold stud earrings and necklace, and the cream gold-bordered sari in the old drape with no blouse. Nagoji at right leans on the table and faces her in profile. He has his topknot, grey temples, curled moustache, clean chin, gold ear stud, white coat, red waistcoat, chain and sword. All four hands are sound. The map has no lettering and the red banner is plain. Slips: (1) The royal seat with its red bolster stands empty in the centre background. Varma sits there in 3.1, 3.2 and 4.1, though 3.4 (already kept) has the same empty dais in soft focus. (2) The background guards wear red turbans and red waist sashes. In 3.1 and 3.2 they wear white head cloths and crossed belts. (3) The map is colour-washed, which matches 3.1 but not the ink map in 3.2. (4) Nagoji is still leaning on both palms rather than fully straightened. None of these breaks a principal, the beat or a hard rule. All three balloons fit on the plain cream wall between the pillars at top centre: Padmini's on the left half, Nagoji's two on the right half, with the rafters above as overflow.

Minor only: in the soft background at right, a dais with a cushion and a spear beside it is empty, a small continuity slip against Varma being present in 3.1 and 4.1. A tiny pen-like scribble on the curled corner of the background map (about 20 px, near x 0.85, y 0.95) could be cleaned in retouch. Otherwise it matches the beat: tight on her large, anatomically sound fist clenched on the head of the stick, her face above it, eyes fixed on Nagoji off-panel right. She has grey threading, gold earrings, necklace and bangle, and the cream gold-bordered sari with no blouse. Both balloons fit on the rafters and wall at upper left, or on the plain wall at right between the window slits.

Small problems only. Varma matches the V13 face: moustache, red tilak, pearl ear drop, bare-headed, bare-chested, cream gold-bordered mundu, gold necklaces. His knot sits at the back right of his head, not above the left ear. This is close to the crown knot already accepted in 3.1. He stands right at the front edge of his platform, with the red-cushioned seat and his tall spear behind him. He drags the tip of a second, short spear along the canal toward the drawn fort mark. That short spear looks a little stubby, but the beat reads clearly. His eyes glance off-panel to the right. The crowd is gone. Only two small Nair guards with crossed belts stand by the doorway. The map is ink and wash only: palms, canal and fort outline, with no lettering. The hall, the light and the brass lamps match page 3 and 4.3. Both balloons fit on the plain back wall in the upper band, at upper left above the doorway or upper right beside his head.

Small problems only. Padmini matches her sheet and the ch26 row: grey threading in her coiled hair, gold ear studs and necklace, bangles, cream gold-bordered sari in the old drape with no blouse, and her rough walking stick. Her hands are sound. Her head and eyes turn sharply toward the right edge, where the king is off-panel. The empty platform is out of frame, and there are no extra people. The cloth map on the waist-high table shows only ink lines. A few faint, smudgy terrain scribbles near its top-right corner, around x 0.85 to 0.95 and y 0.70 to 0.78, read as hill hatching rather than letters. The hall matches 4.3: carved pillars, plain wall, slit window, brass lamps with open flames, and a sunlit doorway. A large plain wall in the upper right takes both balloons well clear of her face.

Small problems only. Nagoji matches his sheet: thick curled moustache, a clean chin, grey at the temples, a Kerala topknot with long curls, and a small gold ear stud. He wears the white European-cut coat, red waistcoat, brass buttons and silver chain of office, with both sleeves down and no brand or scar showing. Faint stubble shading along his jaw and chin could be lightened in retouch. A red cloth sash is wrapped around the waistcoat at the waist; that is not in the bible row or in 3.1, though it reads as part of the waistcoat, red on red. The coat has small shoulder tabs. His head dips in a nod with his eyes down and his jaw set, so the beat reads. The crowd is gone. In soft focus behind him, Varma sits on his platform, which fits the bible and 4.1. Here Varma has a gold-bordered cloth over one shoulder, and the two guards wear red waist sashes, both minor background differences. Brass wall lamps have open flames. The map shows only pictograms and the canal, with no lettering. Both balloons fit on the plain upper-right wall and roof, well clear of his face.

Acceptable with minor notes. Nagoji matches the sheet and the ch25-27 uniform row: Kerala topknot, grey temples, thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, small gold ear stud, white European coat, red waistcoat, brass buttons, silver chain, talwar hilt, boots. Kayal is a bay with black mane, tail and lower legs, no white markings, ochre quilted pad, though her chest reads a little heavy. The column has a red standard with a silver conch, Travancore riders in white mundu with crossed belts, smoke columns and drifting sparks on a red road. No painted text. Minor issues: Ponnan rides on Nagoji's right, not his left (mirrored from the script). Ponnan wears a small gold ear stud of his own, which is Nagoji's identifier. Ponnan's hair is longer and his face leaner than the cropped-curl sheet. He has a foot in a dark shoe or boot. The smoke sits behind and to the right of the column rather than clearly ahead. Lettering: both captions fit in the open sky at the top left (x 0.20 to 0.45, y 0.02 to 0.14, between the standard and Nagoji's head). The smoke at the top right (x 0.65 to 0.98, y 0.02 to 0.15) also works. Neither spot covers a face.

Usable with minor deviations. The riders are painted in full colour instead of silhouette, only Nagoji and Ponnan are shown rather than the reined-in column, and the vantage is only slightly raised, so it reads less as looking down from a ridge. The raiders are also quite close to the riders. Everything else checks out: Nagoji matches in profile (topknot, grey, clean chin, moustache, stud, uniform, chain), Kayal is plain bay with no markings, and Ponnan is correct. The pepper rows, the bare-chested raiders in head cloths with musket smoke, the loaded boats on the canal and the small leaf-swallowed shrine all match the script. There is no painted text and no gore. The caption fits in the sky and distant-hill band across the top centre and right.

Usable. The memory faces are more solid painted portraits than the smoke-textured stain the script asks for, though they are muted, grainy and dissolve into the smoke at their lower edges. Revathi's grey threading is faint but present, and a pendant at her throat reads as the tali. Padmini is greyed, with the stick head beside her. The soldier wears a white turban, unlike the bare-headed riders in 5.1. A few distant structures burn beyond the canal, which is acceptable as the raiders' fires. Nagoji is correct on foot at an untouched green vine line, in the full uniform with clean chin and stud, and the scar is on his left forearm. Dry leaf litter is under his boots and the torch handoff hands are sound. There is no text. The caption fits in the open sky at top left.

Acceptable. The panel matches the beat: tight on the oil-cloth-wrapped torch held to dry leaf litter and bark at the base of a pepper support tree, with flame touching but nothing caught. Nagoji's face behind it is warm-lit and grim, waiting. He matches the sheet: topknot, grey temples, thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, gold ear stud, white coat, red waistcoat, brass buttons, silver chain, buckled boot. No text. Minor notes: under the torch, only the thumb of his second hand peeks out between the coat and the leaves, a small odd blob that is not distracting at print size. The torch flame licks a little way up the bark. Loaded boats sit on the canal in the background. Lettering: the single caption fits in the clear blue sky at the top left (x 0.06 to 0.38, y 0.02 to 0.16), away from his face and the torch.

Clean. Nagoji matches the sheet and the ch25-27 row: topknot, grey at the temples, thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, gold ear stud, sooty white coat, red waistcoat, brass buttons, silver chain, breeches and buckled boots. He steps back from the burning post with the torch raised, and white steam shows at the stem. Shrine, canal and pepper boats match 6.2 to 6.4. One nit: a faint pale smudge about 25 px wide on the inner right wrist of the torch arm looks like faint glyph strokes when zoomed 10x. At print size (1:1) it is only a tiny smudge. Optional retouch. No lettering is needed.

Acceptable. The beat reads: a raised view of separate post fires with gaps between them, Nagoji walking the row with a torch, and Travancore men (white mundu, crossed belts) lighting post after post on either side. His face matches the sheet (stud, clean chin, moustache, topknot, grey temples). The long thin white scar is correctly on his inner LEFT forearm. Minor continuity point: his coat has no soot here, although 6.1 shows soot 'already' on it. The Travancore men wear white head cloths. Their white mundu and crossed belts still set them apart from the raiders. Caption space is the smoky sky at top centre and right (x 0.38 to 0.95, y 0 to 0.07), above the canal treeline.

Acceptable. Fire has leapt from the burning vines onto a pile of fallen branches, with black smoke boiling up. Two Travancore men (white mundu, crossed belts) flinch back from the heat with sound hands and anatomy. The canal, boats and shrine continue 6.1 and 6.2. Minor point: two boatmen in the background (one poling, one seated in a boat) look unbothered by the fire. The long caption can sit in the clear blue sky at top centre-right (x 0.45 to 0.8, y 0 to 0.18).

Acceptable. Travancore musketeers kneel in a line at the edge of the burn and fire into the smoke. They wear white mundu and crossed leather belts, with no blue or red coats. Raiders show as dark head-clothed silhouettes against the flame under a plain, unlettered faded-green banner. Minor points: the raider silhouettes look like they wear tunics rather than bare shoulders. The locks read more like flintlocks than clear matchlocks, which is not noticeable at this scale. Caption space is the smoky sky at top left and centre (x 0.17 to 0.55, y 0 to 0.12).

Acceptable. This fixes the v01 rejection: both coat sleeves now reach his wrists, and neither the hauling hand nor the free hand has any scrawl, scar or marks. Nagoji matches the sheet and the ch25-27 row: soot-streaked face, thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, small gold ear stud, topknot, grey at the temples, a sooty white coat, red waistcoat with brass buttons, silver chain (the medallion has a vague engraving and no letters), knee breeches and buckled boots. He hauls a coughing Travancore man (white head cloth, white mundu, crossed leather belts) out of the smoke by his shoulder cloth. The hands are sound. Raiders behind him cough and stumble with arms over their faces, there are no bodies, and the plain faded-green banner has no writing. The pepper vines, canal, shrine and boats match 6.1 to 6.4. Minor points: (1) the two raiders at right are lit and detailed (bare-chested, indigo cloth, head cloths) rather than pure silhouettes, and one has a single cloth strap over one shoulder, not crossed belts. (2) Small background boatmen in orange head cloths load pepper calmly, the same oddity noted in 6.3. Space for both captions: the smoky sky at top centre (x 0.45 to 0.78, y 0.0 to 0.26), between Nagoji's hair and the banner and above the raiders' heads.

Minor: the distant survivors walk upright carrying spears and a long gun instead of limping. The wading figure's grey short-sleeved shirt, back straps and round cap look slightly modern, and the straps could be read as Travancore cross-belts. All of them are tiny at print size. Everything else is on script: a burned corridor through standing pepper, fallen charred posts, a dropped flintlock and a scorched plain green banner with an unlettered pale disc. There are no bodies and no text, and the sky across the top has clear room for both captions.

Minor only. Nagoji's face is broader and heavier than the sheet, with faint shading on the chin, but every identity marker holds: topknot, grey temples, thick curled moustache, clean chin, gold ear stud. The ch24 uniform is complete: white coat with soot-black cuffs, red waistcoat, brass buttons, breeches, boots and silver chain. He holds the brass cup at chin height with a sour sidelong look, which reads as the grimace. Varma is bare-headed with a knot, cream and gold, gold necklaces, on the far dais. Padmini stands in the side doorway with grey in her hair, soot on her sari and her stick. Soldiers in white mundu line the hall and turn toward her. Brass open-wick lamps. The map has no lettering and there is no painted text. The caption fits in the low-detail ceiling band at top left (x 0 to 0.45, y 0 to 0.13), above every head.

Minor background inconsistencies. A seated figure who resembles Varma wears a cream upper cloth with a gold sash and loose hair, and sits at the table level instead of bare-chested on his platform; he can read as an unnamed councillor. The guards wear white turbans with red sashes, unlike 7.2's bare-headed soldiers. The coat shows no soot, but the cuffs are out of frame. Nagoji himself matches his sheet and the bible row: thick curled moustache, a clean chin with only light hatching, small gold ear stud, grey at the temple, topknot, white coat, red waistcoat and silver chain. His troubled gaze toward frame right fits 7.2's geography, with Padmini on the right. There is clear wall, window and doorway space at upper right (about x 0.59 to 0.80, y 0.03 to 0.35) for both balloons.

Minor only. Padmini matches her sheet and the ch26 row: grey through her coiled hair, cream sari with gold border, old drape, stick. The soot visibly falls from her fingers onto the canal lines. The map is plain ink with no lettering, but it is untinted, while the maps in 8.2 and 8.3 have pale blue water. Her sari shows no soot smear, which matches 7.3 and 7.4. The dim dais at the back of the hall is empty, although Varma is on his platform in 8.3. Put the balloons over the ceiling and back wall at upper right.

Acceptable. Padmini stands at the doorway with her bare back to the hall, in profile toward the night outside, not looking round, her hand sound on her stick. Nagoji is small in the lamplight behind her: crown knot, moustache, clean chin, gold stud, white coat, red waistcoat, chain, breeches and boots. The hall is now empty of soldiers and Varma, and the royal seat at the back is empty, which is a mild break from 8.3; it reads as her isolation. The map scribble has no lettering. Put the three balloons on the ceiling rafters and the back wall in the upper left and centre, clear of both heads.

Minor only. Nagoji has a light stipple of stubble on the jaw and chin. It is within the bible's 'light stubble at most' and matches 9.2 to 9.5. Two spear guards stand by the tower door, so he is not strictly 'alone', but they are distant, facing away and the same as in 9.2, 9.3 and 9.5. The blackened strip shows only as a dark band of distant trees with a bare clearing in front. That fits 'a dark line across the green' but is less obviously burned than the smoking strip in 9.3. Uniform, topknot, grey temples, ear stud, chain, Revathi's indigo sari, jasmine braid, grey threading, sandalwood line, tali and armlets all match. Hands are sound and there is no painted text. The open sunset sky between the tower and Nagoji (top left to centre) takes the caption and Revathi's balloon, and the sky at top right is also clear.

Minor only. Nagoji is walking beside her and glancing at her rather than turning at the parapet, but the panel still reads as him turning to her while she keeps walking. Revathi has a thin red line in her hair parting that is not on her sheet or in 9.3. Both principals otherwise match: Nagoji has a clean chin, curled moustache, gold stud, topknot, grey temples and the uniform with chain; Revathi has grey threading, jasmine braid, sandalwood line, tali, coin necklace and armlets. Open sky at top centre and top right for both balloons.

Minor. The background guards wear white head cloths, while in 9.1 and 9.2 they are bare-headed. Revathi stands at Nagoji's frame-left here, while 9.2 and 9.5 put her at frame-right. Faint smoke still rises from the strip a few days later, which reads as smouldering. The beat is correct: both lean on the parapet staring at the blackened strip and neither looks at the other. Hands are sound. Both match their sheets and bible rows. Wide open sky at the top for her two balloons.

Acceptable with one small detail flag. The pendant on the silver chain of office is a European-style crest: a crown over a shield with two rampant lion supporters. It is not text, but it could read as a European royal arms. At small-panel print size it is a grey disc, so a light retouch to a plain or conch-marked medallion is optional. Nagoji has light jaw stubble, consistent with the rest of the page. He looks off-panel right toward where Revathi stands in 9.5. Topknot, grey temples, curled moustache, ear stud, white coat, red waistcoat and brass buttons all match. The visible hand is anatomically sound. The open sky at top right takes the single balloon easily.

Minor only. Nagoji has light jaw stubble, consistent with the page. Background spear guards at the tower are the same as in 9.1 to 9.3. The script beat is met: Revathi faces the setting sun with warm last light on her face, and Nagoji stands at the left edge in uniform watching her. Her costume matches the sheet and the ch26 row (indigo sari with gold, jasmine braid, grey threading, sandalwood line, tali pendant, armlets). Hands on the parapet are sound and there is no painted text. The wide sunset sky from the centre to the right edge takes all three Revathi balloons without covering faces.

Minor only. Her torso still faces the camera, with only her head and eyes turned to frame right toward the off-panel Nagoji. 'Facing him fully' is softened, but it reads correctly because 10.2 puts Nagoji at her right. She stands beside the parapet rather than visibly straightening from it. There is a thin orange sindoor line in her hair parting, the same small mark she has elsewhere on the page. Everything the r1 correction asked for is fixed: the ink-and-wash rendering and muted lavender-gold sky match 10.2 and 10.3, she has clear grey threading, there is no nose stud, and the tali shows on its dark cord below the flat-coin necklace. Jasmine braid, sandalwood line, armlets, bangles and the indigo-and-gold sari are on model. The same tiled gatehouse and white-mundu guards with crossed belts stand at left, and the burned strip shows as a dark band on the land. Hands are sound. There is no text, and a wide open sky at upper right gives room for both balloons away from her face.

Minor. Nagoji is mid-sized in the frame rather than 'small'. Revathi walks to frame left, back toward the gatehouse she came from in 9.1, which is a screen-direction flip after 10.3 and 10.4. Otherwise it delivers the beat: she walks away along the wall walk, back straight and already small; Nagoji is alone at the parapet under a reddening sky. Both are on model (topknot, grey, moustache, clean chin, ear stud, coat with chain, breeches, boots; jasmine braid, armlets, indigo sari). No text, sound hands, and the same fort and gatehouse as the rest of the scene.
Clean against sheets, bible row and script beat.

Minor only. Ibrahim sits and gestures openly with one hand, which is a little more animated than 'talking quietly'. The scar is thin but clearly visible running from his LEFT ear to his jaw, with the camera on his anatomical left side. Everything else matches the script and his sheet: white turban, grey-flecked beard, teal short coat over a vest with bulging pockets, the stocky build, the canal bank at dusk, a moored boat, stacked cloth bales, and a contact seen from behind in shadow. Both hands are sound and there is no painted text. The open dusk sky across the top centre (about x 0.27 to 0.78, y 0 to 0.18) holds both captions without touching a face.

Minor. The brand on Nagoji's inner LEFT forearm, bare because both sleeves are pushed to the elbow as in 11.3, is painted as a small dark ring-shaped mark next to the white scar. Earlier bible rows describe a pale puckered patch. It has no letters, numerals or cross and is small at print size, but the author may want it checked. Nagoji has light stubble texture. Otherwise the beat is right: a two-shot at the map table, Nagoji leaning in with both hands on the table, Ramayyan writing and not looking up. The hall, uniform, chain and gold stud match 11.3, the guards wear white mundu with crossed belts, the map and leaves have no text, and the hands are sound. There is clear space top-left (doorframe and sky above the guard) for Nagoji's balloon and on the ceiling and wall above Ramayyan for his.

Minor only. The turned palm leaf curls into a soft cone, more pliant than real dried palm leaf. A few peppercorns in the dish read reddish-brown rather than fully black. The beat is otherwise right: a tight shot on Ramayyan's hands in ivory cloth, one turning a leaf while the brass stylus moves on the next line, and a brass dish of peppercorns weighting the bound stack of finished leaves. Hand anatomy is sound and no letters are incised or painted on the leaves. The background is the same laterite-and-timber war hall by day as 11.3 and 11.4. The blurred upper band (the dark wall at top left-centre and the pillars and window at top right) leaves room for both captions above the hands and the dish.
